Marathon Petroleum stock was essentially flat today—up just 0.13%—but sits 7.5% higher over two weeks as refiners benefit from sustained elevated crude prices and tight refinery capacity. US oil is trading at $97.26 per barrel while Brent (the global benchmark) has climbed near $108, driven by ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Iranian attacks in the Gulf, which have kept investors worried about supply disruptions. Refineries are running at 97.8% capacity, close to maximum, which means Marathon and peers can push margins wider when crude prices stay elevated and global demand remains strong.

The geopolitical tension in the Middle East—particularly the Iran war backdrop and pipeline disruptions in Saudi Arabia—has kept oil prices firm for weeks. That's the real engine behind the refiner's steady climb: when crude stays expensive and refineries can't run much harder, the difference between what crude costs and what refined products sell for becomes the key lever for profit, and that spread has been favorable.
